newsitem.title: UK: West warns Bosnian leaders to stick to peace terms.
newsitem.headline: West warns Bosnian leaders to stick to peace terms.

text.p: An international conference on implementing peace in Bosnia ended on Thursday with a warning to Bosnian leaders that future Western aid depends on their compliance with the peace agreement they signed a year ago.

"The conference agreed on a set of specific conclusions, placing clear obligations on the parties and setting out the extent of the support the international community is ready to continue to provide," the British Foreign Office said.

The conference agreed to give more support to the international war crimes tribunal at the Hague, including extra resources, and issued a renewed commitment to the Bosnian reconstruction programme, said the Foreign Office document.
The two-day talks, grouping more than 50 nations, were called to assess progress on the Bosnian peace deal clinched in the United States a year ago.
Frustration over repeated delays in implementing the civilian aspects of the so-called Dayton agreement has led Western leaders to link aid to a renewed commitment to genuine peace on the ground.
Among the most contentious issues is the fate of indicted war criminals, the vast majority of whom remain at large despite evidence of genocide and other crimes against humanity.
